title: Implement a Dry-Run Mode for Data Ingestion Pipelines
description: The HermesHEAL platform processes large batches of sensitive healthcare data. Operators and data engineers need a way to validate pipeline configurations and preview the ingestion process without actually executing the resource-intensive and data-altering steps. This task involves introducing a '--dry-run' command-line flag that will simulate a pipeline run, printing informational messages about the steps that would be taken.

project_spec.name: HermesHEAL Unified Healthcare Data Lake Platform
project_spec.description:
HermesHEAL is an expert-level monolithic C application that consolidates hospital, laboratory, wearable, imaging and pharmacy feeds into a single, regulation-compliant data lake. At its core it implements a high-throughput ETL pipeline that performs real-time data_ingestion from HL7/FHIR streams and nightly batch_processing of EHR extracts. Integrated data_validation, data_quality_checks, error_recovery and data_transformation stages normalize disparate clinical vocabularies (LOINC, SNOMED-CT, ICD-10) and de-identify PHI in compliance with HIPAA. Parallel_processing is achieved with a custom thread-pool and lock-free ring buffers that power stream_processing of telemetry such as ICU vitals, while a scheduler orchestrates long-running genomics loads and retrospective analytics jobs.

A built-in observer-based monitoring subsystem continuously audits ingest latency, transformation accuracy and storage capacity, emitting events to an internal Event_Streaming bus used by the Strategy_Pattern-driven alert engine to trigger automated remediation workflows (e.g., rollback corrupted batches or re-hydrate cold storage). The monolith offers a unified CLI, REST façade and embedded data_visualization dashboards so clinical researchers can explore longitudinal patient cohorts without context-switching across services. By combining Data_Lake, Pipeline_Pattern and ETL_Pipeline concepts inside a single deployable artifact, HermesHEAL eliminates cross-service network hops—crucial for low-latency clinical decision support and strict on-premise deployment policies common in healthcare institutions.
dependencies: libpq (PostgreSQL client) – metadata, audit and configuration storage
Apache Arrow C library – in-memory columnar data representation for fast transformations
Apache Parquet C++ (linked via C FFI) – efficient columnar file storage inside the lake
libhv – lightweight HTTP/REST server for admin APIs and visualization feed
cJSON – fast JSON parsing/serialization for HL7/FHIR payloads
libevent – high-performance event loop supporting stream_processing and scheduling
OpenSSL – encrypted data-at-rest and in-transit, TLS termination
Prometheus C client – time-series metrics export for monitoring
SQLite – embedded config & local queue persistence for error_recovery buffers
zstd – compression for cold archival tiers
